hello.note: Literally 'are you well?'; Isan's all-purpose greeting.

good_morning.note: Isan has no separate morning greeting.

good_evening.note: Works at any hour, evening included.

goodbye.note: Literally 'good luck', softened with the ender der.

how_are_you.native: เป็นจั่งใด
how_are_you.note: Literally 'is however?'; a casual 'how's it going'.

thank_you.note: Literally 'thank heart, much'; everyday Isan thanks.

youre_welcome.note: Literally 'glad'; shared with Lao nyin dee.

no_problem.native: บ่เป็นหยัง
no_problem.note: Literally 'not being anything'; matches Lao baw pen nyang.

please.note: Formal, shared with Thai; day to day often just der.

yes.note: Isan's affirmative 'right/correct', distinct from Thai chai.

no.note: The word that most marks Isan speech; replaces Thai mai.

of_course.note: Same root as Thai; casually paired with 'yu laew'.

amazing.note: Literally 'beautiful, very'; praise for anything great.

delicious.note: Isan's famous 'delicious' word, now known nationwide.

cheers.note: Literally 'clink glass'; shared toasting custom with Lao.
